topic.title: GPay is the word, UPI is the thing
topic.claim: When we say 'GPay kar do' for any UPI payment, one brand has won the one thing no ad can buy: becoming the word.
topic.behaviour: People say 'GPay kar do' whichever app they use. A Karan Johar story about a school snack counter that took 'only GPay' is the latest example.
topic.mechanism: The first app people learned becomes the name of the act. After that, rivals have to spend money on a habit that is already owned.
topic.group: Everyday UPI users who pay with PhonePe, Paytm or a bank app and still say 'GPay'
topic.moment: You're paying with PhonePe, but you tell the shopkeeper 'GPay kar diya'.

turn.believed: We pick the app that is best for us.
turn.actually: We pick the name that is already in our mouth, and the brand that owns the word owns the habit.

topic.villain: a market where the first brand to teach a habit gets the name of the habit for free
topic.because: Once a brand name becomes the verb, every payment by any app is free advertising for the first one. Rivals have to fight a word, not a product.

proof.fact: The article uses Karan Johar's school sports day anecdote, where the snack counter took only Google Pay, to show how 'GPay kar do' is said for any UPI payment, whichever app people use.

topic.payoff: Check your own habit: which app do you say out loud, and is it the one you actually use?
topic.send_to: The friend who still says 'GPay kar do' while paying with another app.
real_details: The anecdote came from Koffee with Karan season 9
topic.news_peg: Karan Johar's 'Only GPay' anecdote from Koffee with Karan season 9, reported on 7 November 2026
topic.why_now: The anecdote went around this week and prompted a fresh look at how a brand name becomes a verb.

score.why: Everyone says 'GPay kar do' while paying with another app. A brand becoming the word is a clear hidden win, and the anecdote supports it without being the point.
